source.title: How Vision Transformers Represent Position: A Mechanistic Comparison of Absolute and Rotary Positional Encodings
source.authors: Mahmoud Mannes; Nikhil Maturi; Parva Mehta; Jiwon Jeong; A. Kannappan

record.file_problem: none; the full paper and appendices are present.
record.tranche_reason: The study does not test feature superposition, but its own SAE results refine the scope of V5: selected SAE features capture causal positional structure in APE models, yet do not account for all decodable position, and SAE reconstruction or feature ablation is unreliable for the tested RoPE models.
record.gate_note: The paper studies positional representations in vision transformers, not sparse-feature superposition or polysemanticity. Only SAE results that bear on whether SAE features capture positional information are included. Other positional-encoding, probe, and classification results do not test the listed versions. No values from cited work are included.
record.test_reason: The study uses SAEs as a tool to localise position in vision transformers, but its own controls bear on V5 (dictionary completeness and faithfulness). In APE ViTs, position stays probe-decodable from the SAE error after the positional features are removed. In a RoPE ViT, SAE reconstruction alone distorts the measured structure. This is incidental evidence from a new setting (vision, positional features), so T3 rather than T5. The study gives no explicit argument against V5.
record.authors_conclusion: Correct. The authors also state that the features explain the spatial structure and most of its classification effect, but not everything a probe can read.
record.recipe_differences: This is a mechanistic study of positional encoding in vision transformers using SAE feature edits and RoPE rotation masking; it does not reproduce a superposition method.
record.method_sensitivity: The reported SAE findings differ by positional encoding: selected APE features are useful for isolating positional structure, while SAE reconstruction and ablation are unreliable for the tested RoPE models.

fits_no_version.finding: APE vision transformers store position in about 20 of 3,840 SAE features, row- and column-selective, that tile the grid. RoPE models show no such features (max selectivity 3.4 vs 5.2–9.8).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Whether a model's representation is SAE-decomposable into interpretable sparse features depends on architecture (e.g., positional-encoding scheme).

record.problems: Evidence is limited to ViT-B and ViT-S models at 224×224 in the main analyses. The authors state that APE SAE features do not account for all decodable position and that SAE reconstruction is unreliable on RoPE; the RoPE DINOv3 SAE ablation did not reach the prespecified usability threshold.
record.rows_left_out: The paper's many additional positional-encoding probe, rotation-masking, patching, and ImageNet-classification results were left out because they do not test the listed superposition versions or SAE-feature completeness beyond the included rows.

untested.parts: Stability across seeds or dictionary sizes, canonicality, and features beyond position are not tested. Only one SAE per model (TopK, 3,840 latents) was trained.
Not tested: toy models, sparsity transition, geometry.
Not tested: alternative causes of polysemanticity.
Not tested: no LLMs (vision transformers only).
Not tested: the row and column features are not analysed for dimensionality.

missing.what: Probe accuracy after zeroing the positional features without the error added back (16.6/5.9/28.4/8.8%). This contrast with r5–r8 isolates the position held in the SAE error.
Held-out SAE fraction of variance unexplained, 0.114–0.142, and dead latents 0–5.7%.
Ridge row/column R2 after own-axis ablation stays 0.13–0.71, so per-axis position lies outside the screened features.
SAE reconstruction alone lowers the DINO probe from 95.9 to 82.1% (rerun 99.9 to 96.8%).

record.verdict_notes: This is a vision-transformer study of positional encoding. The SAE evidence on V5 is incidental and concerns only positional features. Restricting V4 to LLMs excludes these ViT results from it.

versions.untested_parts: Toy-model superposition, feature overlap geometry, sparsity-dependent transitions, and regular geometry are not tested.
Capacity competition as an explanation for polysemantic neurons is not tested.
Alternative causes of polysemantic neurons and whether polysemanticity indicates superposition are not tested.
The study uses vision transformers, not LLMs; it does not test feature spread across LLM neurons or SAE recovery in LLMs.
The study tests SAE recovery of positional information in these vision models, not whether SAE features are stable or canonical units across tasks, datasets, or model representations generally.
The dimensionality of features in superposition is not tested.

rows.subject: supervised ViT-B
rows.operation_detail: Zeroed the selected positional SAE features at block 2, adding the SAE reconstruction error back.
rows.note: The edit substantially reduces positional structure, but the paper reports that SAE features do not capture all decodable position.
rows.check: Correct values from Table 7 (SSDC 0.76 intact, 0.25 after zeroing with error added back). The features carry most but not all of the SSDC structure; random and matched-random controls leave SSDC at 0.76.

rows.subject: naver ViT-B
rows.operation_detail: Passed residual activations through the SAE and back without editing features.

conditions.value: residual stream; maximum reported across blocks not stated

rows.measure: Change in SSDC from SAE reconstruction
rows.baseline: SSDC without SAE reconstruction; exact value not stated
rows.note: The authors describe reconstruction alone as shifting SSDC enough to make the SAE an unreliable intervention for RoPE.
rows.check: Reconstruction alone raises SSDC by up to 0.214 on naver ViT-B, against 0.062 and 0.065 on two APE models (App. D.7). The SAE reconstruction does not faithfully preserve the representation here. The baseline should name the APE comparison values.

source_check.correct: state=partial for V5: reconstruction distorts positional structure, demonstrating imperfect representation rather than absence of represented information.
source_check.locator_found: Section 4.3 and Appendix D.7: naver ViT-B reconstruction alone raises SSDC by up to 0.214.
source_check.problem: The reconstruction shift establishes limited fidelity; it does not establish that dictionary representation is wholly absent.

rows.subject: DINOv3 ViT-B
rows.operation_detail: Zeroed 22 SAE features, the largest dose tried.
rows.note: The reduction was below the paper's prespecified 30% drop required for a usable edit; the authors say the SAE approach does not transfer reliably to RoPE models.
rows.check: The weak SSDC drop (0.948 to 0.863) may reflect that RoPE stores no positional residual-stream features, which is the authors' reading, rather than an SAE failure. The row cannot separate the two explanations.

relationships.condition: APE ViT-B models, positional features at block 2
relationships.reason: Screened SAE features carry most or all of the SSDC structure (r1–r4). Yet with the error added back, exact position stays 57–93% decodable (r5–r8), so the dictionary is incomplete.
relationships.display_finding: Screened SAE features carried most or all of the SSDC structure, yet with the SAE error added back exact position stayed 57–93% decodable, so the dictionary was incomplete.

relation.reason: Although SAEs serve as an investigative tool, the study also reports its own controls demonstrating incomplete capture and reconstruction distortion relevant to V5.

tranche.reason: The study's reconstruction-error controls and RoPE reconstruction distortion directly qualify V5 completeness and fidelity; T5 captures these findings more specifically than a new-setting classification.

source_check.notes: The authors' conclusion is accurately paraphrased. These results concern the tested SAEs and positional information; dictionary stability and canonicality are untested.

statements.correction: V5 label for this study: limits_scope. Block-2 exact-position accuracy after positional-feature zeroing with SAE error added back: supervised 67.2%; DINO 84.4%; AugReg 93.2%; SAM 57.0%. SSDC remains 0.25, 0.07, 0.09 and 0.23, respectively.
statements.problem: The study-specific facts are correct, but the challenges label overstates evidence of incomplete capture, which warrants limits_scope under the verdict rules.

reader_labels.label: limits_scope
reader_labels.condition: APE models, positional information at block 2
reader_labels.reason: Selected SAE features capture and causally affect positional structure, but substantial exact-position information remains probe-decodable after their removal; this qualifies any claim that the dictionary features are complete units of the representation (r1–r8).

reader_labels.label: limits_scope
reader_labels.reason: SAE reconstruction shifts SSDC substantially on naver ViT-B, and the largest tested DINOv3 feature ablation has only a limited effect; the paper concludes SAE-based position analysis is unreliable for these RoPE models (r9–r10).
